lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've had the best trip ever! Today, our adventure goes underground. The old map is glowing, and it points to a cave. When a place has no light, you can say, It's dark in here. Then, you can say, Turn on your flashlight. Say it with me. It's dark in here. Turn on your flashlight. Great! In a dark place, always stay close to a grown-up. Never go into a real cave alone. Let's read the sign at the cave door. "Welcome to the Cave of Riddles! It's dark inside, so bring a flashlight. Stay with your group, and walk slowly. Listen carefully. This cave is full of secrets and riddles. Can you solve them all? From Luma, the cave keeper." What should you bring? A flashlight. Who is the cave keeper? Luma. Now, phonics. Darkness. Brightness. Softness. Coldness. Dark becomes darkness. Bright becomes brightness. Add n, e, s, s, and the word becomes a thing. Let's step into the darkness together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's dark in here. Turn on your flashlight. Today, we're standing in a big hall in the cave. Let's describe it. There's a small door at the back of the cave. Say it with me. There's a small door at the back of the cave. Great! Use there's for one thing, and there are for two or more things. There are lots of lamps on the walls. Where is it? At the front, in the middle, at the back. Let's read Luma's welcome sign. "This is the Great Hall. There's a stone table in the middle. There are twelve lamps on the walls. At the back, there's a small door, but it's locked. The key is hidden somewhere in the cave. Good luck, young detectives!" What's in the middle of the hall? A stone table. Can we open the small door? No, it's locked. Now, phonics. Sadness. Happiness. Kindness. Weakness. Happy becomes happiness. Change y to i, then add ness. Let's describe the Great Hall!

In the top left corner, there's a bat. In the top right corner, there's a gold crown. In the bottom right corner, there are three stars. In the center, there's a big moon. Look carefully. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In the top left corner, there's a bat. Today, we'll play a game called Describe and Draw. One person describes a picture. The other person listens and draws. Listen for the position words. Next to, under, on, behind, between. There's a lamp next to the box. Say it with me. There's a lamp next to the box. Super! If you're not sure, ask a question. Is the box big or small? Let's read the game card. "Describe and Draw. Player A: Look at the picture, but don't show it. Describe it in five sentences. Player B: Listen and draw. You can ask three questions. Then, compare the two pictures. Are they the same? Have fun!" How many sentences does Player A say? Five. How many questions can Player B ask? Three. Now, phonics. Fairness. Cleverness. Laziness. Tidiness. Lazy, laziness. Tidy, tidiness. Change y to i before ness. Now, find a partner. Let's describe and draw!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, There's a lamp next to the box. Today, we'll make a map of the cave. A good map shows where things are. At the end of the tunnel, there's a lake. Say it with me. At the end of the tunnel, there's a lake. Great! Now we can use all our words: at the back, in the middle, next to, and at the end of. We can give directions, too. Go straight, and turn left. Let's read Kiko's cave map notes. "From the entrance, go straight. There are two tunnels. Take the left tunnel. Turn left at the big rock. At the end of the tunnel, there's an underground lake. The Great Hall is on the right. There's a small door at the back of the hall." Which tunnel do we take? The left tunnel. What's at the end of the tunnel? A lake. Now, phonics review. Darkness. Kindness. Happiness. Laziness. Remember, happy becomes happiness, and lazy becomes laziness. Let's draw our cave map!

phonics.tipJa: ive を つけると「〜する せいしつの」の ことば。act → active、create → creative（e を とって ive）、detect → detective（たんてい）、invent → inventive。英語の ことばは v で おわらないので、さいごの e を わすれずに。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, At the end of the tunnel, there's a lake. Today, we're walking in a dark passage. Shh! Listen. Flap, flap, flap. What's that sound? We don't know for sure. So we can say, It might be a bat. Say it with me. What's that sound? It might be a bat. Great! Might means maybe. Use it when you're not sure. It might be the wind. It might be water. Let's read a page from Luma's cave guide. "Sounds in the Cave. Drip, drip: It might be water from the ceiling. Whoosh: It might be the wind in the tunnels. Flap, flap: It might be Bella the bat. She flies around at night. Don't worry. She's very friendly." What might drip, drip be? Water from the ceiling. Who is Bella? A friendly bat. Now, phonics. Active. Creative. Detective. Inventive. Act, active. Create, creative. These words end in v and e. Let's listen like careful detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What's that sound? It might be a bat. Today, Kiko found something shiny between two rocks. It's small and gold. It has a round top and little teeth. We're almost sure what it is. So we can say, It must be a key. Say it with me. It's small and gold. It must be a key. Excellent! Might means maybe. Must means I'm almost sure. Let's read the note next to the rocks. "Clever explorer, you found it! This small gold thing is old and very special. It opens something in the Great Hall. Don't lose it, and don't give it to anybody. Use it at the right time. From Luma." What does it open? Something in the Great Hall. So, it must be the key to the small door! Now, phonics. Expensive. Explosive. Impressive. Attractive. Expense, expensive. Explode, explosive. The d changes to s. Let's find more clues and use them well!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's small and gold. It must be a key. Today, Birimo is scared. He heard a long, low sound. Whoooo! Is it a ghost? No! When something is impossible, we say, It can't be. It can't be a ghost. Ghosts aren't real! Say it with me. It can't be a ghost. Ghosts aren't real! Great! Remember: it must be means almost sure, yes. It can't be means almost sure, no. Let's read the poem on the cave wall. "In the cave, the wind can sing. Whoooo, whoooo, a scary thing! But listen well, and you will hear: it's only wind, so have no fear. Your voice comes back from far away. That's an echo, so please stay!" What makes the whoooo sound? The wind. What is an echo? Your own voice coming back. Now, phonics. Protective. Descriptive. Decorative. Massive. Describe, descriptive. Decorate, decorative. When a friend is scared, say kind words. Let's be brave together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It can't be a ghost. Ghosts aren't real! Today, we found big footprints in the mud. How sure are we? We have three useful words. Maybe means about fifty percent. Probably（たぶん） means about eighty percent. Definitely means one hundred percent. It's probably a bear's footprint. Say it with me. It's probably a bear's footprint. Great! But good detectives always check the clues again before they decide. Let's read Haru's notebook. "The footprint is very big and long. There are no claws. There's a pattern of lines, like the bottom of a shoe. Next to the footprints, there's some fresh dirt. So, it's definitely not a bear. It's probably a big boot!" Are there claws? No. What's next to the footprints? Fresh dirt. Who loves digging in the dirt? Mr. Mole! Now, phonics. Talkative. Imaginative. Defensive. Supportive. Talk, talkative. Imagine, imaginative. Here, the ending is ative. Let's check our clues!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's probably a bear's footprint. Today, we'll play a guessing game. There's something in Luma's bag. You can touch it, but you can't look. Then, say your guess and a reason. It might be a ball because it's round. Say it with me. It might be a ball because it's round. Great! Remember our three words. Might is maybe. Must is almost sure, yes. Can't is almost sure, no. Let's read the game rules. "Guess the Object. Put your hand in the bag. Touch the object, but don't look. Say one thing about it, like It's soft or It's round. Then, make a guess with might, must or can't. Give a reason with because. Three right guesses win a prize!" What can't you do? Look. Which word do we use for a reason? Because. Now, phonics review. Sadness. Brightness. Detective. Expensive. Imaginative. Ness makes a thing word, and I, V, E makes a describing word. Let's guess like detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we played a guessing game with a mystery bag. Today, we go deep into the cave and look for clues. A detective says, Look at these footprints. Someone was here. Say it with me. Look at these footprints. Someone was here. Great! Someone means a person or an animal, but we don't know which one. Let's read a note from Luma, the glowworm keeper of the cave. "Welcome to the deep hall, explorers. Please walk slowly. The floor is wet near the lake. Yesterday evening, I cleaned the floor, so it was perfectly clean. Please tell me about anything new on the floor." Was the floor clean yesterday? Yes, it was. So, if we see footprints today, someone was here after Luma cleaned. That's a clue! Ask your friend, Whose footprints are they? You can answer, They might be Mr. Mole's. Now, phonics. Footprint. Foot and print. Flashlight. Flash and light. Somebody. Some and body. Fingerprint. Finger and print. Two small words make one long word. Let's look for clues like real detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Look at these footprints. Someone was here. Today, something terrible happens in the cave. Luma's Crystal Crown is missing! We can say, The crown was here yesterday. Now it's gone. Say it with me. The crown was here yesterday. Now it's gone. Good! Gone means not here anymore. Let's read the sign next to the glass box. "The Crystal Crown. This crown is the treasure of the Cave of Riddles. It shines in the dark like a hundred stars. Please look, but do not touch. Every evening at six, Luma checks the crown." When does Luma check the crown? At six. Yesterday morning, the crown was in the box. But at six o'clock, the box was empty. What happened to the crown? Nobody knows the answer yet. But don't worry. It must be somewhere in the cave. Must means we are almost sure. Now, phonics. Nobody. No and body. Somewhere. Some and where. Everywhere. Every and where. Something. Some and thing. Let's look everywhere for the crown!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The crown was here yesterday. Now it's gone. Today, we'll talk to the animals in the cave. Luma thinks the crown disappeared at about three o'clock. So, a detective asks, Where were you at three o'clock? Say it with me. Where were you at three o'clock? Great! To answer, we say, I was sleeping, or, I was reading. Let's read Luma's list of the cave animals. "Cave animals: Mr. Mole lives in a tunnel under the big rock. Bella the bat sleeps on the ceiling in the daytime. Pip the bluebird sings by the waterfall. Cora the crow loves shiny stones. Everyone was in the cave yesterday afternoon." Who sings by the waterfall? Pip does. Who loves shiny stones? Cora does. Hmm. That's interesting. After the first answer, ask one more question. What were you doing then? Write every answer in your notebook. Now, phonics. Keyhole. Key and hole. Footstep. Foot and step. Moonlight. Moon and light. Waterfall. Water and fall. Let's ask good questions, detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we asked, Where were you at three o'clock? Today, we'll talk to a witness（もくげきしゃ）. A witness saw something happen. We can ask, Do you know who took it? Say it with me. Do you know who took it? Wonderful! Look carefully. We don't say, Do you know who did take it. We say, Do you know who took it. You can also ask, Do you know where Cora is? If you don't know the answer, say, Sorry, I don't know. Let's read Pip's words in our notebook. "Pip the bluebird: At three o'clock, I was singing by the waterfall. Then I saw a black bird. It flew fast toward the lake. It had something shiny in its beak. Maybe it was a stone, but I'm not sure." What color was the bird? Black. Where did it fly? Toward the lake. What did it have in its beak? Something shiny. Now, phonics. Doorway. Door and way. Staircase. Stair and case. Bookshelf. Book and shelf. Notebook. Note and book. Let's ask our witness!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we asked, Do you know who took it? Today, let's put all our clues on a clue board. Say it with me. Clue 1: wet footprints. Clue 2: a blue feather. Good job! Let's read our clue board together. "Clue 1: wet footprints. They are small, and they have three toes. They go from the glass box to the lake. Clue 2: a blue feather. It was next to the empty box. Clue 3: Pip saw a black bird with something shiny." Now, let's think together. Three toes. Those are bird feet! Mr. Mole has big paws, so it can't be Mr. Mole. The feather is blue, so it might be Pip. But wait. Pip saw a black bird. Hmm. That's strange. A good detective doesn't decide too fast. Look at every clue again, and say, It might be, or, It can't be, with a reason. Now, phonics review. Footprint. Foot and print. Flashlight. Flash and light. Darkness. Dark and ness. Creative. Create, drop the e, add i, v, e. Let's check every clue, detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we made a clue board. Today, the wet footprints lead us to a big stone door. There are words on the door. It's a riddle! Let's read it together. "I am the Riddle Door. I have heard a thousand riddles. Answer my riddle, and I will open. Riddle one: It has four legs, but it can't walk. You eat your dinner on it. What is it?" What do you think? Say it with me. It has four legs, but it can't walk. Hmm. A dog has four legs, but a dog can walk. So, it can't be a dog. You eat dinner on it. It's a table! Riddles use the word but a lot. It has a face, but it can't smile. It has teeth, but it can't eat. Can you guess them? Now, phonics. Some words have similar meanings. Silent and quiet. Scared and afraid. Strange and weird. Clever and smart. Use different words, and your riddles will sound more interesting. Let's open the Riddle Door!

"Riddle two: The more you take, the more you leave behind. You make me with your feet. You can see me in the snow, in the sand and in the mud. What am I?" Say it with me. The more you take, the more you leave behind. Great! If you don't know the answer, you can say, Let me think. Or give me a hint, please. Here's a hint. Take one step. Now, look behind you. What did you leave? Take two more steps. You left more! So, what's the answer? Footsteps! Now, phonics. Similar words again. Begin and start. Finish and end. Quick and fast. Simple and easy. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The more you take, the more you leave behind. Footsteps! The Riddle Door opened, and now we're in a new room. Today, we'll use better words for big and small. Say it with me. It's a huge rock with a tiny hole. Wonderful! Huge means very, very big. Tiny means very, very small. Let's read Riko's notebook. "Behind the Riddle Door, there's a huge room. In the middle, there's an enormous rock. It's as tall as a house. On the rock, there's a tiny hole. Next to the rock, there are giant mushrooms. They glow green in the dark." How tall is the rock? As tall as a house. What color are the mushrooms? Green. Look at the tiny hole. It's shaped like a key. Do we have a key? Yes! We found a gold key in the rock wall. Now, phonics. Huge. Big. Tiny. Small. Giant. Big. Enormous. Big. Huge, giant and enormous are all bigger than big! Use them when you describe a picture. Let's describe this amazing room!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's a huge rock with a tiny hole. There's a riddle contest in the cave soon, so today, we'll write our own riddles. Say it with me. It's yellow. Monkeys love it. What is it? A banana! Let's read Haru's riddle card. "My riddle. Hint 1: I'm long and yellow. Hint 2: Monkeys love me. Hint 3: You peel me before you eat me. What am I?" Here's how to write a good riddle. First, think of an answer. Then, write three hints. Start with a difficult hint, and finish with a simple hint. Don't say the answer in your hints! Try it now. Think of an animal or a food. Is it large or little? What color is it? Where can you find it? Now, phonics. Large and big. Little and small. Glad and happy. Correct and right. When your friend guesses the answer, say, That's correct! Let's write our riddles!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we wrote our own riddles. Today is the Cave Riddle Contest! Let's read the poster. "The Cave Riddle Contest! Tonight at seven in the Mushroom Hall. Bring your best riddle. Read it loudly and clearly. The audience will guess the answer. The cleverest riddle wins a glowing stone. Everyone is welcome!" Where is the contest? In the Mushroom Hall. What time does it start? At seven. What's the prize? A glowing stone. Say it with me. I'm round. I have a face, but no eyes. Great! The audience can ask, Are you a clock? Answer, Yes, I am, or, No, I'm not. If your riddle is too difficult, give a tiny hint. Listen kindly to every riddle, and clap for your friends. Now, phonics review. Huge. Big. Tiny. Small. Footstep. Foot and step. Kindness. Kind and ness. Read your riddles loudly and clearly. Let the contest begin!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we made our own riddles and had a riddle contest. Today, we'll play a guessing game called Twenty Questions. One person thinks of an animal or a thing. The others ask yes or no questions. Listen. Is it bigger than a box? No, it isn't. It's smaller than a box. Can it fly? Yes, it can. Say it with me. Is it bigger than a box? Great! Good detectives ask big questions first, and then small questions. Let's read the rules on a stone in the cave. "Twenty Questions. Think of an animal or a thing. Your friends can ask twenty questions. You can only answer yes or no. Ask about size, color and what it can do. If your friends guess the answer, they get a shiny stone!" How many questions can you ask? Twenty. How can you answer? Only yes or no. Now, phonics. Listen to the end of each question. Is it bigger than a box? It goes up. What is it? It goes down. Can it fly? Up. Where does it live? Down. Yes or no questions go up. Questions with what or where go down. Let's play Twenty Questions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we played Twenty Questions. Is it bigger than a box? No, it isn't. Today, we'll use yes or no questions to find the thief. Remember, the crown was in the glass box yesterday. Now it's gone. When we ask about the past, we say, Was the thief tall? No, it wasn't. It was small. Did it have wings? Yes, it did. Say it with me. Was the thief tall? Wonderful! Every answer helps us. A small thief with wings. Now our list of suspects is shorter. Let's read a note from Luma, the glowworm keeper of the cave. "Yesterday afternoon, I heard a sound near the crown. I saw a small shadow on the wall. It moved very fast. Then I heard flap, flap, flap. I was too sleepy to look carefully. Please help me find my crown!" What did Luma see? A small shadow. What did she hear? Flap, flap, flap. Now, phonics. Was the thief tall? Up. Who took the crown? Down. Did you see anything? Up. What color was it? Down. Let's ask more questions, detectives!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we asked yes or no questions. Was the thief tall? No, it wasn't. Today, someone thinks Haru took the crown! When you know it's not true, you can say, It can't be Haru. Then, give a reason. He was with me. Say it with me. It can't be Haru. He was with me. Excellent! A good detective listens to other ideas, too. Ask kindly, Why do you think so? Are you sure? Then explain your reason. Let's read a page from Riko's notebook. "Three o'clock: Haru and I were at the waterfall. We took a photo of a rainbow. Pip was singing nearby. Three thirty: we walked back to the big hall with Kiko. Six o'clock: Luma told us the crown was gone." Where was Haru at three o'clock? At the waterfall with Riko. So, can it be Haru? No! It can't be Haru. Now, phonics. Where were you? Down. Were you with Haru? Up. Why do you think so? Down. Are you sure? Up. Let's give good reasons!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, Riko said, It can't be Haru. He was with me. Today, we'll solve the mystery! When you know the answer, say it clearly, and give a reason. The thief was the crow! It loves shiny things. Say it with me. The thief was the crow! Great! Your friends may ask, How did you know? Then, connect the clues. Let's read Kiko's detective notebook. "Clue 1: wet footprints with three toes. A bird walked by the lake. Clue 2: a blue feather. But crow feathers look blue in the lamp light. Clue 3: crows love shiny things. Answer: Cora the crow took the crown!" How many clues did Kiko find? Three. Why did the feather look blue? Because of the lamp light. In the end, Cora gave the crown back and said sorry. She only wanted to watch it shine. Now, phonics. Do you know who took it? Up. How did you know? Down. Does it like shiny things? Up. When did it happen? Down. Let's explain our answers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we were picture detectives. In this picture, something is strange. Today, you'll write your own mystery story. A good mystery has three parts. The beginning. Something disappears. One night, the museum's painting disappeared. The clues. The next morning, a guard found a clue. And the answer. In the end, the painting was in the storeroom. Say it with me. One night, the museum's painting disappeared. Wonderful! Let's read my example story. "One night, the museum's famous painting of a cat disappeared. Nobody heard anything. The next morning, a guard found a clue. There was a tiny trail of white paint on the floor. It went to the storeroom door. In the end, the painting was in the storeroom. A painter was fixing the cat's whiskers!" What disappeared? The painting of a cat. Where was the clue? On the floor. Now, phonics review. Happiness. Imaginative. Nobody. Begin. Where did it go? Down. Now, begin your story. Be imaginative!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we wrote our own mystery stories. One night, the museum's painting disappeared. Today, we'll take one last walk through the Cave of Riddles. Let's use everything we learned. To describe places, say, There's a light at the end of the tunnel. To guess, say, It might be a bat. It must be the wind. It can't be a ghost! Say it with me. There's a light at the end of the tunnel. Great! At the end of our walk, Luma gave us a letter. Let's read it. "Dear detectives, thank you for finding my crown. Your kindness and your clever questions helped everyone in the cave. Cora and I are good friends again. Please take this invitation. Follow the echoes. They will take you to the Theater of Echoes. Love, Luma." What did Luma give us? An invitation. Where will the echoes take us? To the Theater of Echoes. Now, phonics review. Kindness. Detective. Flashlight. Huge. Was it the crow? Up. Let's say goodbye to the cave!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we took a goodbye walk through the cave. There's a light at the end of the tunnel. Today is the big riddle show in the great hall. Everyone in the cave is here. Luma, Mr. Mole, Bella, Pip and Cora are in the audience. First, Haru tells a riddle. Then, we play Twenty Questions. Finally, Kiko explains the crown mystery. At the end, we all shout, The case is closed! Great detective work! Say it with me. The case is closed! Great detective work! Fantastic! Let's read the poster for the show. "Riddle Show Tonight! Place: the great hall of the Cave of Riddles. Time: seven o'clock. Riddles, Twenty Questions, and the true story of the missing crown. Bring your flashlight and your clever ideas. Everyone is welcome!" Where is the show? In the great hall. What should you bring? A flashlight and clever ideas. Now, phonics. Darkness. Creative. Footprint. Giant. Who did it? Down. Is the case closed? Up. Let's start the riddle show!

segments.subtitleJa: たんていの ぼうしを ちょっと あげて。こんにちは！ こんどは ステージを かいちゅうでんとうで てらして。
segments.subtitleEn: Tip your detective hat. Hello! Now shine your flashlight on the stage.

slide.title: Let's move!
items: Shine your flashlight on the stage.

segments.say: Speed challenge! Hat! Flashlight! Stop! Go! Now clap for all the detectives!
segments.subtitleJa: スピード チャレンジ！ ぼうし！ ライト！ とまって！ いって！ さあ、たんてい みんなに はくしゅ！
segments.subtitleEn: Speed challenge! Hat! Flashlight! Stop! Go! Now clap for all the detectives!

slide.title: Let's move!
items: Shine your flashlight on the stage.

segments.say: Repeat after me. The case is closed!
segments.subtitleJa: まねして いってね。「じけんは かいけつ！」
segments.subtitleEn: Repeat after me. The case is closed!

segments.say: Great detective work!
segments.subtitleJa: 「みごとな たんていの しごと！」
segments.subtitleEn: Great detective work!

segments.say: Thank you for coming to our riddle show!
segments.subtitleJa: 「わたしたちの なぞときショーに きて くれて ありがとう！」
segments.subtitleEn: Thank you for coming to our riddle show!

slide.title: Say it!
items: Thank you for coming to our riddle show!

segments.say: Your turn! Make a tiny riddle for your family. Give one clue. What is it? When they guess, say, The case is closed!
segments.subtitleJa: あなたの ばん！ おうちの ひとに ちいさな なぞなぞを つくろう。ヒントを ひとつ だして。「なーんだ？」 あたったら「The case is closed!」と いおう！
segments.subtitleEn: Your turn! Make a tiny riddle for your family. Give one clue. What is it? When they guess, say, The case is closed!

segments.say: Quiz time! The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they? A, footsteps. B, cookies. Think!
segments.subtitleJa: クイズ！ とれば とるほど、うしろに のこして いく ものは なに？ A、あしあと。B、クッキー。かんがえて！
segments.subtitleEn: Quiz time! The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they? A, footsteps. B, cookies. Think!

slide.title: Quiz
items: Welcome to our riddle show! Here's a riddle. The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?

segments.say: It's A! Footsteps! Every step leaves a footprint behind. Great detective work!
segments.subtitleJa: こたえは A！ あしあと！ ひとあし ごとに あしあとが のこるね。みごとな たんていの しごと！
segments.subtitleEn: It's A! Footsteps! Every step leaves a footprint behind. Great detective work!

segments.say: The case is closed! You can describe, guess, ask and explain like real detectives. Next, go and talk with Riko! Then, on to World 26, the Theater of Echoes! See you!
segments.subtitleJa: じけんは かいけつ！ ほんものの たんていの ように、せつめいして、すいりして、しつもんして、はっぴょう できるね。このあと リコちゃんと おはなし してね！ そのあとは ワールド26、ひびきの げきじょうへ！ バイバイ！
segments.subtitleEn: The case is closed! You can describe, guess, ask and explain like real detectives. Next, go and talk with Riko! Then, on to World 26, the Theater of Echoes! See you!

slide.title: Today's wrap-up
items: Thank you for coming to our riddle show!
